name: Eyedropper
howItWorks: The nib section unscrews from the barrel and the barrel itself becomes the ink tank. You fill it with a glass dropper, then screw the section back.
pros: Very large ink capacity and no moving parts.
cons: Can leak at the threads, and filling is messy.

name: Crescent filler
howItWorks: A crescent-shaped ring on the barrel presses a bar against a rubber sac inside. Press, dip the nib in ink, release: the sac springs back and pulls ink in.
pros: Self-contained and quick; no loose parts.
cons: The sac eventually perishes and needs replacing.

name: Lever filler
howItWorks: A small lever on the side lifts a pressure bar that squeezes a rubber sac. Lift the lever, dip the nib, lower the lever, and the sac fills with ink.
pros: Simple, reliable and easy to use.
cons: Holds less ink than a piston; sacs age.

name: Button filler
howItWorks: A button at the end of the barrel pushes a pressure bar against the sac. Press the button, dip the nib, let go, and ink is drawn in.
pros: Neat: no side lever to catch on a pocket.
cons: The sac must be replaced when it hardens or splits.

name: Plunger filler
howItWorks: A rod with a seal on the end slides inside the barrel like a syringe. Push it down to expel air, dip the nib, pull it up to draw ink in.
pros: Holds a lot of ink and works without a rubber sac.

name: Vacuum filler
howItWorks: Pressing a plunger flexes a diaphragm inside the barrel. Released with the nib in ink, the diaphragm pulls ink up and in.
pros: Large capacity and fast to fill.

name: Piston filler
howItWorks: Turning a knob at the end of the barrel moves a piston along a thread. Turn one way to push air out, dip the nib, turn the other way to draw ink in, like a syringe.
pros: High capacity, no sac to perish, and ink level can be seen in clear barrels.
cons: More parts and more costly to build.

name: Snorkel filler
howItWorks: A thin tube slides out of the nib unit and dips into the ink, so the nib stays clean. A plunger action then draws ink up the tube.
pros: Clean: the nib never touches the ink.
cons: Complicated, so repairs are specialist work.

name: Aerometric filler
howItWorks: A flexible sac sits inside a metal sleeve. Squeeze the sleeve to flatten the sac, dip the nib, and release it so the sac pulls ink in.
pros: Sealed unit that is easy to refill.
cons: Capacity is limited by the sac size.

name: Capillary filler
howItWorks: Narrow channels inside the filler pull ink upward by capillary action when the nib is dipped in ink. No squeezing is needed.
pros: Clean and quick; no sac to fail.
cons: Smaller capacity and unusual to repair.

name: Cartridge / converter
howItWorks: A sealed ink cartridge is pushed onto a pin that pierces it. A converter is a refillable cartridge with a small piston, so you can use bottled ink.
pros: Cleanest and easiest to use, and ideal for travel.
cons: Brand-specific sizes, and each cartridge holds only a little ink.
